recipes.title: Easy Rotisserie Chicken Noodle Soup
recipes.description: A one-pot shortcut soup with rotisserie chicken, Amish egg noodles, and a butter finish. Deep, cozy flavour without a whole day at the stove.
recipes.imageAlt: Flat Bauhaus-style illustration of a white bowl of chicken noodle soup with steam

ingredients.note: start with 1/2 tsp; recommended for depth

steps: Shred or chop all the rotisserie chicken meat and set it aside.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the carrots, celery, and onion and sauté for 4–5 minutes, until the onion is soft and translucent.
Pour in the Swanson broth. Stir in the liquid aminos, fish sauce (if using), garlic powder, parsley, oregano, thyme, bay leaf, salt, and pepper. Add the shredded chicken.
Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 25–30 minutes, until the carrots are tender.
Remove the bay leaf. Taste the broth and adjust the seasoning — a tiny bit more liquid aminos helps if it tastes flat.
Stir in the Amish egg noodles. Cook for 8–12 minutes, checking early, until just al dente. They cook faster than regular pasta and will keep softening in the hot broth.
Optional thickening: ladle about 1 cup of hot broth into a bowl, whisk in the cornstarch until smooth, then stir it back into the pot. Simmer for 1–2 minutes.
Turn off the heat. Stir in the butter until melted — this gives the soup its classic rich finish without making it heavy.
Taste one last time and adjust the salt or pepper. Add a splash more broth if the noodles have absorbed too much liquid.
recipes.notes:
Slow cooker: Add everything except the noodles, cornstarch, and butter to the slow cooker. Cook on Low for 6–8 hours or High for 4–6 hours. Stir in the Amish egg noodles and cook until al dente, usually 15–25 minutes — check early. Turn off the heat, stir in the butter, and thicken with a cornstarch slurry if desired.

The liquid aminos and the small amount of fish sauce deepen the chicken flavour without tasting soy-forward or fishy. The butter at the end is the classic finishing touch. Amish egg noodles absorb a lot of liquid, so keep extra Swanson broth on hand for leftovers — the soup thickens as it sits, and reheats best with a splash more broth.

recipes.title: Sheet Pan Birria Tacos
recipes.description: Crispy, golden quesabirria tacos with tender chile-braised beef, melted cheese, and warm consomé for dipping. The sheet pan does the hard part.
steps: Remove the stems and seeds from the dried chiles and place them in a heatproof bowl. Cover with hot water and soak for 15–20 minutes.
Pat the beef chuck roast pieces dry and season generously with kosher salt.
Turn the pressure cooker to the sauté setting, add a drizzle of neutral oil, and sear the beef on all sides until nicely browned. Remove and set aside.
Add the tomatoes and onion straight into the pressure cooker and sear until golden. Remove and set aside.
Strain the chiles, reserving the soaking water.

Add the chiles to a blender with the tomatoes, onion, garlic, oregano, cumin, coriander, apple cider vinegar, kosher salt, black pepper, and about 1 cup of the chile water. Blend until completely smooth.
Return the seared beef to the pressure cooker. Pour the blended sauce through a fine mesh strainer over the top, using a spoon or spatula to push it through, and discard the solids left behind.
Add the beef broth, bay leaves, and cinnamon stick. Pressure cook on high for 1 hour, then allow a natural release of the steam.
Preheat the oven to 450°F. Transfer the beef from the pressure cooker to a bowl and shred it.
Strain the consomé left in the pressure cooker once more into a small pot and keep it warm on the stove. Stir about 1/2 cup of the warm consomé into the shredded beef.

Dip each tortilla in the consomé so it coats both sides, then place it on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Add the shredded beef and some torn or shredded Oaxaca or mozzarella cheese. Press firmly to seal, holding for a few seconds if needed so the tacos stay closed, then cover with a little more cheese. Bake for about 15 minutes, until golden and the cheese is bubbly.
Serve with the remaining consomé for dipping, plus lime wedges, cilantro, and diced white onion.

recipes.title: Chocolate Olive Oil Cake
recipes.description: A one-bowl chocolate cake with a tender, almost brownie-like crumb. Olive oil keeps it moist for days and makes it taste grown-up.
recipes.imageAlt: A thick slice of dark chocolate layer cake with chocolate drizzle and cream on a white plate.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a 9-inch round cake pan, line the bottom with parchment, and grease the parchment.

In a large bowl, whisk the flour, cocoa, baking soda, and salt. Add the sugar, olive oil, eggs, milk, and vanilla. Whisk until smooth, then slowly whisk in the hot espresso. The batter will be thin — that is correct.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan and bake for 35–40 minutes, until the centre springs back and a skewer comes out with just a few moist crumbs.
Cool in the pan for 15 minutes, then turn out onto a rack to cool completely.
Dust with powdered sugar just before serving. Slice with a hot, dry knife for clean edges.
recipes.notes: The cake is even better on day two, wrapped tightly at room temperature. It also freezes well for up to two months. Serve with slightly sweetened whipped cream or a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
